rows: Windows job objects manage groups of processes as a unit and can terminate associated processes together.
Breakaway policy and job membership must be explicitly configured and verified.
TerminateJobObject terminates all processes associated with a job, including child jobs in a hierarchy.
Only associated processes are covered; permissions and breakaway behavior matter.
AssignProcessToJobObject binds a process to an existing job object.
Existing job membership and required access rights must be handled.
JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE can terminate associated processes when the final job handle closes.
This requires the extended limit structure and correct job membership.
Start-Process launches processes; with -Wait it waits for the process tree.
Waiting does not by itself provide identity, timeout or kill-on-timeout receipts.
Wait-Process waits only for specified process objects or IDs, unlike Start-Process -Wait process-tree behavior.
A direct PID wait cannot prove descendant cleanup.
Stop-Process terminates processes selected by ID or name.
Stopping a parent PID alone does not prove every descendant has stopped.
Get-CimInstance queries CIM classes such as Win32_Process.
Application logic must validate exact fields rather than broad substrings.
Win32_Process exposes PID, parent PID, executable path, command line and creation information.
Consumers must bind these fields to the intended invocation.
File.Replace replaces a destination with another file and can preserve a backup.
Atomic publication still needs same-volume, validation and durability policy.
FileStream Flush(true) writes buffered data through intermediate file buffers.
Directory-entry durability and schema validation remain separate requirements.
Child processes inherit process-scope environment variables.
Runner execution must sanitize and record the effective inherited environment.
Execution policy Bypass blocks nothing and provides no prompts or warnings.
Pinned script and executable identity remain necessary.
PowerShell applies expression and argument-mode quoting rules, especially for paths with spaces.
External-process argument construction requires exact round-trip tests.
git fetch downloads objects and updates remote-tracking references; atomic reference updates can be requested.
Fetched remote identity and exact target commit must still be authenticated.
git remote manages named repositories and can report configured remote URLs.
A runner should pin the canonical repository identity before fetch and push.
Git configuration controls remotes, hooks, credentials and safe-directory behavior.
Recovery should use a bounded trusted configuration and record effective settings.
git stash stores worktree and index state; --include-untracked also includes untracked files.
The exact newly created stash object and its covered paths must be verified.
git rev-parse resolves repository roots, Git directories and revision names.
Resolved values must be tied to the intended repository and invocation.
Porcelain status is intended for script-oriented worktree state inspection.
The snapshot must be durably preserved before mutation.
git worktree manages multiple working trees linked to one repository.
Worktree identity and pruning require containment and ownership checks.
git update-ref supports reference updates with expected-old-value checks.
File-level CAS and remote publication still require coordinated transaction semantics.
The current INSPIRE files were published 5 July 2026 and are replaced on the first Sunday monthly.
Catalogue presence does not prove downloaded GML bytes.
EA documents DTM 1m in EPSG:27700 with ±0.15m RMSE; OS Terrain 50 remains a coarse secondary screen.
Fresh WCS and Terrain 50 package bytes still require hashes and exact row receipts.
